addedToCycleAt.description: Conditions on when the issue joined its current cycle. Changing cycles resets this time; removing the cycle clears it.

addedToCyclePeriod.description: Conditions on when the issue joined its cycle. before includes the cycle’s first 24 hours; during covers the remaining time before closure, and after covers times at or after closure.

ageTime.description: Age (created -> now) comparator, defined if the issue is still open.

and.description: Conditions that the issue must all match. These are combined with the other fields in this filter.

archivedAt.description: Conditions on when the issue was archived. Also set includeArchived on the query; a filter alone does not include records excluded by the query’s archive setting.

assignee.description: Conditions on the assigned user. For example, null: true finds unassigned issues, while id: { eq: "user-uuid" } selects one assignee.

attachments.description: Conditions on the issue’s external links. For example, some with a URL or sourceType condition finds issues with at least one matching attachment.

autoArchivedAt.description: Conditions on when the issue was automatically archived. Include archived issues in the query to find them; restoring an issue clears this value.

autoClosedAt.description: Conditions on when the issue was automatically closed after inactivity. The value is cleared when its status changes.

canceledAt.description: Conditions on when the issue entered a canceled or duplicate status. The value is cleared when the issue leaves those status types.

children.description: Conditions on direct sub-issues. Use some for a matching child, every for all children, or length to count them. This does not search all descendants recursively.

comments.description: Conditions on comments linked directly to the issue, including replies. Inline comments on the issue description are linked through documentContent and are not included by this filter.

completedAt.description: Conditions on the recorded completion time. Use null: false to require a completion time, or a date range to find issues completed during that period.

createdAt.description: Filters by creation time. Use a fixed timestamp or a relative duration, such as `{ gte: "-P7D" }` for resources created in the last seven days.

creator.description: Filters that the issues creator must satisfy.

customerCount.description: Conditions on the number of distinct customers with active requests linked to the issue. Requests without a customer record each count separately. Supply one comparison; to apply a range, put separate customerCount conditions in and.

customerImportantCount.description: Conditions on the number of distinct customers with active, important requests linked to the issue. Important requests without a customer record each count separately. Supply one comparison; to apply a range, put separate customerImportantCount conditions in and.

cycle.description: Conditions on the assigned cycle. Use null: true for issues without a cycle or whose team has cycles disabled. Use null: false to require an assigned cycle on a team with cycles enabled. Other cycle comparisons do not require cycles to be enabled.

delegate.description: Filters that the issue's delegated agent must satisfy.

description.description: Conditions on the issue’s stored description text. Use null to find issues without a stored description, or text comparisons to match its contents.

dueDate.description: Conditions on the due date, without a time of day. Use null: true for issues without a due date.

estimate.description: Conditions on the stored numeric estimate in the team’s scale. Use null to find unestimated issues; zero is a separate, explicit estimate.

hasActiveAgentSessions.description: Comparator for filtering issues bucketed as having active agent sessions, no closed agent pull requests, and no merged agent pull requests.

hasBlockedByRelations.description: Whether another issue blocks this issue, with both issues still open. A link with a closed issue counts under hasRelatedRelations instead.

hasBlockingRelations.description: Whether this issue blocks another issue, with both issues still open. A link with a closed issue counts under hasRelatedRelations instead.

hasDismissedAgentSessions.description: Comparator for filtering issues bucketed as having all agent sessions dismissed or closed, and no merged agent pull requests.

hasDuplicateRelations.description: Whether other issues have been marked as duplicates of this issue. This checks incoming duplicate links, not whether this issue is itself a duplicate.

hasErroredAgentSessions.description: Comparator for filtering issues bucketed as having an errored agent session, no active sessions, and no merged agent pull requests.

hasMergedAgentPullRequests.description: Comparator for filtering issues which have agent-session-linked pull requests that were merged.

hasRelatedRelations.description: Whether the issue has a related link in either direction. Blocking links also count as related when either issue is closed; open blocking relationships are covered by hasBlockingRelations and hasBlockedByRelations.

hasSharedUsers.description: Comparator for filtering issues which have been shared with users outside of the team.

hasSuggestedAssignees.description: Comparator for filtering issues which have suggested assignees.

hasSuggestedLabels.description: Comparator for filtering issues which have suggested labels.

hasSuggestedProjects.description: Comparator for filtering issues which have suggested projects.

hasSuggestedRelatedIssues.description: Comparator for filtering issues which have suggested related issues.

hasSuggestedSimilarIssues.description: Comparator for filtering issues which have suggested similar issues.

hasSuggestedTeams.description: Comparator for filtering issues which have suggested teams.

id.description: Matches the issue UUID or human-readable identifier, such as ENG-123. Use number with a team filter when matching only the numeric portion.

labels.description: Conditions on assigned labels. Use some for at least one matching label, every to constrain all labels, or length: { eq: 0 } for unlabeled issues. Separate some conditions in and can require different labels on the same issue.

lastAppliedTemplate.description: Filters that the last applied template must satisfy.

needs.description: Conditions on customer requests linked to the issue. Use some to require a matching request or length to count linked requests.

number.description: Matches the issue number within its team. Numbers are not unique across teams, so combine this with team when looking for a specific issue.

or.description: Alternative conditions; the issue must match at least one. Other fields at this level must still match. An empty list adds no condition.

parent.description: Conditions on the immediate parent issue. Use null: true to find top-level issues, or an ID condition to find direct sub-issues of one parent.

priority.description: Conditions on the numeric priority: 0 = No priority, 1 = Urgent, 2 = High, 3 = Medium, 4 = Low. Lower nonzero values mean higher priority.

project.description: Conditions on the assigned project. Use null: true for issues without a project; otherwise the project must match the supplied conditions.

projectMilestone.description: Filters that the issues project milestone must satisfy.

reactions.description: Conditions on emoji reactions added directly to the issue. Reactions on its comments are filtered through comments.reactions.

recurringIssueTemplate.description: [ALPHA] Filters that the recurring issue template must satisfy.

releases.description: Conditions on releases linked to the issue. An issue can belong to several releases; use some to require a matching release or length to count them.

sharedWith.description: Filters that users the issue has been shared with must satisfy.

slaBreachesAt.description: Conditions on the SLA deadline. A deadline before now does not by itself mean the SLA was missed; use slaStatus to distinguish unfinished breaches from completed outcomes.

slaStatus.description: Conditions on the current SLA risk or outcome. Use null: true for issues without an SLA status, including canceled issues and issues without an SLA.

snoozedBy.description: Filters that the issues snoozer must satisfy.

snoozedUntilAt.description: Conditions on when the issue’s triage snooze ends. Use null: true for issues without a recorded snooze time.

sourceMetadata.description: Filters that the source must satisfy.

startedAt.description: Conditions on when work started. Use null: true for issues with no recorded start time; moving back to triage, backlog, or an unstarted status clears it.

state.description: Conditions on the issue’s current status. Filter by type, such as started or completed, to match the same workflow category across teams with different status names and IDs.

subscribers.description: Filters that issue subscribers must satisfy.

suggestions.description: Filters that the issue's suggestions must satisfy.

team.description: Filters that the issues team must satisfy.

title.description: Conditions on the issue title. This does not search descriptions or comments.

triagedAt.description: Conditions on when the issue last left triage. The value is unset before triage is completed and after re-entering triage.

hasDismissedAgentSessions.description: Comparator for filtering issues bucketed as having all agent sessions dismissed or closed, and no merged agent pull requests.

hasDuplicateRelations.description: Whether other issues have been marked as duplicates of this issue. This checks incoming duplicate links, not whether this issue is itself a duplicate.

hasRelatedRelations.description: Whether the issue has a related link in either direction. Blocking links also count as related when either issue is closed; open blocking relationships are covered by hasBlockingRelations and hasBlockedByRelations.

hasSharedUsers.description: Comparator for filtering issues which have been shared with users outside of the team.

id.description: Matches the issue UUID or human-readable identifier, such as ENG-123. Use number with a team filter when matching only the numeric portion.

labels.description: Conditions on assigned labels. Use some for at least one matching label, every to constrain all labels, or length: { eq: 0 } for unlabeled issues. Separate some conditions in and can require different labels on the same issue.

lastAppliedTemplate.description: Filters that the last applied template must satisfy.

needs.description: Conditions on customer requests linked to the issue. Use some to require a matching request or length to count linked requests.

null.description: Use true to match an unset issue relation, or false to require it to be set. Omit this field when you only want to test the related record’s properties.

number.description: Matches the issue number within its team. Numbers are not unique across teams, so combine this with team when looking for a specific issue.

or.description: Alternative conditions; the issue must match at least one. Other fields at this level must still match. An empty list adds no condition.

parent.description: Conditions on the immediate parent issue. Use null: true to find top-level issues, or an ID condition to find direct sub-issues of one parent.

priority.description: Conditions on the numeric priority: 0 = No priority, 1 = Urgent, 2 = High, 3 = Medium, 4 = Low. Lower nonzero values mean higher priority.

project.description: Conditions on the assigned project. Use null: true for issues without a project; otherwise the project must match the supplied conditions.

reactions.description: Conditions on emoji reactions added directly to the issue. Reactions on its comments are filtered through comments.reactions.

releases.description: Conditions on releases linked to the issue. An issue can belong to several releases; use some to require a matching release or length to count them.

sharedWith.description: Filters that users the issue has been shared with must satisfy.

slaBreachesAt.description: Conditions on the SLA deadline. A deadline before now does not by itself mean the SLA was missed; use slaStatus to distinguish unfinished breaches from completed outcomes.

slaStatus.description: Conditions on the current SLA risk or outcome. Use null: true for issues without an SLA status, including canceled issues and issues without an SLA.

snoozedBy.description: Filters that the issues snoozer must satisfy.

snoozedUntilAt.description: Conditions on when the issue’s triage snooze ends. Use null: true for issues without a recorded snooze time.

sourceMetadata.description: Filters that the source must satisfy.

startedAt.description: Conditions on when work started. Use null: true for issues with no recorded start time; moving back to triage, backlog, or an unstarted status clears it.

state.description: Conditions on the issue’s current status. Filter by type, such as started or completed, to match the same workflow category across teams with different status names and IDs.

team.description: Filters that the issues team must satisfy.

title.description: Conditions on the issue title. This does not search descriptions or comments.

contains.description: Matches strings containing this text. Case-sensitive.

containsIgnoreCase.description: Matches strings containing this text, ignoring case.

containsIgnoreCaseAndAccent.description: Matches strings containing this text, ignoring case and accents.

endsWith.description: Matches strings ending with this text. Case-sensitive.

eqIgnoreCase.description: Matches the full string, ignoring case.

in.description: Values to include in the match. For scalar comparisons, matches any listed value. An empty list matches nothing.

neqIgnoreCase.description: Excludes the full string, ignoring case.

nin.description: Values to exclude from the match. For scalar comparisons, an empty list adds no restriction.

notContains.description: Excludes strings containing this text. Case-sensitive.

notContainsIgnoreCase.description: Excludes strings containing this text, ignoring case.

notEndsWith.description: Excludes strings ending with this text. Case-sensitive.

notStartsWith.description: Excludes strings starting with this text. Case-sensitive.

startsWith.description: Matches strings starting with this text, with case preserved.

startsWithIgnoreCase.description: Matches strings starting with this text, ignoring case.

every.description: Applies each string condition to every item. For example, `{ startsWith: "ENG" }` requires a nonempty array whose items all start with `ENG`. The `in` and `nin` operators compare whole sets of values. Cannot be combined with `some`.

length.description: Compares the number of items using nonnegative integers. Empty and missing arrays both have length zero. This condition must match alongside any `some` or `every` condition.

some.description: Requires a matching item for each supplied string condition; different items may satisfy different conditions. For example, `{ eq: "ENG" }` requires an item equal to `ENG`. Use `nin` to exclude arrays containing any value from a list. Cannot be combined with `every`.

contains.description: Matches strings containing this text. Case-sensitive.

containsIgnoreCase.description: Matches strings containing this text, ignoring case.

containsIgnoreCaseAndAccent.description: Matches strings containing this text, ignoring case and accents.

endsWith.description: Matches strings ending with this text. Case-sensitive.

eqIgnoreCase.description: Matches the full string, ignoring case.

in.description: Values to include in the match. For scalar comparisons, matches any listed value. An empty list matches nothing.

neqIgnoreCase.description: Excludes the full string, ignoring case.

nin.description: Values to exclude from the match. For scalar comparisons, an empty list adds no restriction.

notContains.description: Excludes strings containing this text. Case-sensitive.

notContainsIgnoreCase.description: Excludes strings containing this text, ignoring case.

notEndsWith.description: Excludes strings ending with this text. Case-sensitive.

notStartsWith.description: Excludes strings starting with this text. Case-sensitive.

startsWith.description: Matches strings starting with this text, with case preserved.

startsWithIgnoreCase.description: Matches strings starting with this text, ignoring case.

every.description: Applies each string condition to every item. For example, `{ startsWith: "ENG" }` requires a nonempty array whose items all start with `ENG`. The `in` and `nin` operators compare whole sets of values. Cannot be combined with `some`.

length.description: Compares the number of items using nonnegative integers. Empty and missing arrays both have length zero. This condition must match alongside any `some` or `every` condition.

some.description: Requires a matching item for each supplied string condition; different items may satisfy different conditions. For example, `{ eq: "ENG" }` requires an item equal to `ENG`. Use `nin` to exclude arrays containing any value from a list. Cannot be combined with `every`.

contains.description: Matches strings containing this text. Case-sensitive.

endsWith.description: Matches strings ending with this text. Case-sensitive.

eqIgnoreCase.description: Matches the full string, ignoring case.

in.description: Values to include in the match. For scalar comparisons, matches any listed value. An empty list matches nothing.

neqIgnoreCase.description: Excludes the full string, ignoring case.

nin.description: Values to exclude from the match. For scalar comparisons, an empty list adds no restriction.

notContains.description: Excludes strings containing this text. Case-sensitive.

notContainsIgnoreCase.description: Excludes strings containing this text, ignoring case.

notEndsWith.description: Excludes strings ending with this text. Case-sensitive.

startsWith.description: Matches strings starting with this text, with case preserved.

startsWithIgnoreCase.description: Matches strings starting with this text, ignoring case.

every.description: Applies each string condition to every item. For example, `{ startsWith: "ENG" }` requires a nonempty array whose items all start with `ENG`. The `in` and `nin` operators compare whole sets of values. Cannot be combined with `some`.

length.description: Compares the number of items using nonnegative integers. Empty and missing arrays both have length zero. This condition must match alongside any `some` or `every` condition.

some.description: Requires a matching item for each supplied string condition; different items may satisfy different conditions. For example, `{ eq: "ENG" }` requires an item equal to `ENG`. Use `nin` to exclude arrays containing any value from a list. Cannot be combined with `every`.

description: Returns projects visible to you in the workspace. Use filter to narrow the results and the connection arguments to page or sort them.

after.description: Returns results after this cursor. Pair with `first` and the previous page's `endCursor` to fetch the next page. Keep the filters and ordering unchanged between pages. Cannot be combined with `last` or `before`.

before.description: Returns results before this cursor. Pair with `last` to paginate backward, using a cursor returned by the same connection. Keep the filters and ordering unchanged between pages. Cannot be combined with `first` or `after`.

first.description: The maximum number of results to return, starting after `after` if supplied. Between 1 and 250. Defaults to 50 when neither `first` nor `last` is supplied. Cannot be combined with `last` or `before`.

includeArchived.description: Includes archived resources alongside active ones. Defaults to false, which returns only active resources. This does not include deleted resources.

last.description: The maximum number of results to return, ending before `before` if supplied. Between 1 and 250. Cannot be combined with `first` or `after`.

orderBy.description: Orders results by creation time or last meaningful update time. Defaults to `createdAt`. Results are newest first with `first` and oldest first with `last`; use the returned `endCursor` as `before` to continue backward. Cannot be combined with custom `sort` options on fields that support them.

hasMergedAgentPullRequests.description: Comparator for filtering issues which have agent-session-linked pull requests that were merged.

hasRelatedRelations.description: Whether the issue has a related link in either direction. Blocking links also count as related when either issue is closed; open blocking relationships are covered by hasBlockingRelations and hasBlockedByRelations.

hasSharedUsers.description: Comparator for filtering issues which have been shared with users outside of the team.

hasSuggestedAssignees.description: Comparator for filtering issues which have suggested assignees.

hasSuggestedLabels.description: Comparator for filtering issues which have suggested labels.

hasSuggestedProjects.description: Comparator for filtering issues which have suggested projects.

hasSuggestedSimilarIssues.description: Comparator for filtering issues which have suggested similar issues.

hasSuggestedTeams.description: Comparator for filtering issues which have suggested teams.

id.description: Matches the issue UUID or human-readable identifier, such as ENG-123. Use number with a team filter when matching only the numeric portion.

labels.description: Conditions on assigned labels. Use some for at least one matching label, every to constrain all labels, or length: { eq: 0 } for unlabeled issues. Separate some conditions in and can require different labels on the same issue.

lastAppliedTemplate.description: Filters that the last applied template must satisfy.

needs.description: Conditions on customer requests linked to the issue. Use some to require a matching request or length to count linked requests.

null.description: Use true to match an unset issue relation, or false to require it to be set. Omit this field when you only want to test the related record’s properties.

number.description: Matches the issue number within its team. Numbers are not unique across teams, so combine this with team when looking for a specific issue.

or.description: Alternative conditions; the issue must match at least one. Other fields at this level must still match. An empty list adds no condition.

parent.description: Conditions on the immediate parent issue. Use null: true to find top-level issues, or an ID condition to find direct sub-issues of one parent.

priority.description: Conditions on the numeric priority: 0 = No priority, 1 = Urgent, 2 = High, 3 = Medium, 4 = Low. Lower nonzero values mean higher priority.

project.description: Conditions on the assigned project. Use null: true for issues without a project; otherwise the project must match the supplied conditions.

projectMilestone.description: Filters that the issues project milestone must satisfy.

reactions.description: Conditions on emoji reactions added directly to the issue. Reactions on its comments are filtered through comments.reactions.

sharedWith.description: Filters that users the issue has been shared with must satisfy.

slaBreachesAt.description: Conditions on the SLA deadline. A deadline before now does not by itself mean the SLA was missed; use slaStatus to distinguish unfinished breaches from completed outcomes.

slaStatus.description: Conditions on the current SLA risk or outcome. Use null: true for issues without an SLA status, including canceled issues and issues without an SLA.

snoozedBy.description: Filters that the issues snoozer must satisfy.

snoozedUntilAt.description: Conditions on when the issue’s triage snooze ends. Use null: true for issues without a recorded snooze time.

sourceMetadata.description: Filters that the source must satisfy.

startedAt.description: Conditions on when work started. Use null: true for issues with no recorded start time; moving back to triage, backlog, or an unstarted status clears it.

state.description: Conditions on the issue’s current status. Filter by type, such as started or completed, to match the same workflow category across teams with different status names and IDs.

contains.description: Matches strings containing this text. Case-sensitive.

containsIgnoreCase.description: Matches strings containing this text, ignoring case.

containsIgnoreCaseAndAccent.description: Matches strings containing this text, ignoring case and accents.

endsWith.description: Matches strings ending with this text. Case-sensitive.

eqIgnoreCase.description: Matches the full string, ignoring case.

in.description: Values to include in the match. For scalar comparisons, matches any listed value. An empty list matches nothing.

neqIgnoreCase.description: Excludes the full string, ignoring case.

nin.description: Values to exclude from the match. For scalar comparisons, an empty list adds no restriction.

notContains.description: Excludes strings containing this text. Case-sensitive.

notContainsIgnoreCase.description: Excludes strings containing this text, ignoring case.

notEndsWith.description: Excludes strings ending with this text. Case-sensitive.

notStartsWith.description: Excludes strings starting with this text. Case-sensitive.

startsWith.description: Matches strings starting with this text, with case preserved.

startsWithIgnoreCase.description: Matches strings starting with this text, ignoring case.

every.description: Applies each string condition to every item. For example, `{ startsWith: "ENG" }` requires a nonempty array whose items all start with `ENG`. The `in` and `nin` operators compare whole sets of values. Cannot be combined with `some`.

length.description: Compares the number of items using nonnegative integers. Empty and missing arrays both have length zero. This condition must match alongside any `some` or `every` condition.

some.description: Requires a matching item for each supplied string condition; different items may satisfy different conditions. For example, `{ eq: "ENG" }` requires an item equal to `ENG`. Use `nin` to exclude arrays containing any value from a list. Cannot be combined with `every`.

archivedAt.description: Conditions on when the issue was archived. Also set includeArchived on the query; a filter alone does not include records excluded by the query’s archive setting.

assignee.description: Conditions on the assigned user. For example, null: true finds unassigned issues, while id: { eq: "user-uuid" } selects one assignee.

attachments.description: Conditions on the issue’s external links. For example, some with a URL or sourceType condition finds issues with at least one matching attachment.

autoArchivedAt.description: Conditions on when the issue was automatically archived. Include archived issues in the query to find them; restoring an issue clears this value.

autoClosedAt.description: Conditions on when the issue was automatically closed after inactivity. The value is cleared when its status changes.

canceledAt.description: Conditions on when the issue entered a canceled or duplicate status. The value is cleared when the issue leaves those status types.

children.description: Conditions on direct sub-issues. Use some for a matching child, every for all children, or length to count them. This does not search all descendants recursively.

comments.description: Conditions on comments linked directly to the issue, including replies. Inline comments on the issue description are linked through documentContent and are not included by this filter.

completedAt.description: Conditions on the recorded completion time. Use null: false to require a completion time, or a date range to find issues completed during that period.

createdAt.description: Filters by creation time. Use a fixed timestamp or a relative duration, such as `{ gte: "-P7D" }` for resources created in the last seven days.

creator.description: Filters that the issues creator must satisfy.

customerCount.description: Conditions on the number of distinct customers with active requests linked to the issue. Requests without a customer record each count separately. Supply one comparison; to apply a range, put separate customerCount conditions in and.

customerImportantCount.description: Conditions on the number of distinct customers with active, important requests linked to the issue. Important requests without a customer record each count separately. Supply one comparison; to apply a range, put separate customerImportantCount conditions in and.

cycle.description: Conditions on the assigned cycle. Use null: true for issues without a cycle or whose team has cycles disabled. Use null: false to require an assigned cycle on a team with cycles enabled. Other cycle comparisons do not require cycles to be enabled.

delegate.description: Filters that the issue's delegated agent must satisfy.

description.description: Conditions on the issue’s stored description text. Use null to find issues without a stored description, or text comparisons to match its contents.

dueDate.description: Conditions on the due date, without a time of day. Use null: true for issues without a due date.

estimate.description: Conditions on the stored numeric estimate in the team’s scale. Use null to find unestimated issues; zero is a separate, explicit estimate.

hasActiveAgentSessions.description: Comparator for filtering issues bucketed as having active agent sessions, no closed agent pull requests, and no merged agent pull requests.

hasBlockedByRelations.description: Whether another issue blocks this issue, with both issues still open. A link with a closed issue counts under hasRelatedRelations instead.

hasBlockingRelations.description: Whether this issue blocks another issue, with both issues still open. A link with a closed issue counts under hasRelatedRelations instead.

hasDismissedAgentSessions.description: Comparator for filtering issues bucketed as having all agent sessions dismissed or closed, and no merged agent pull requests.

hasDuplicateRelations.description: Whether other issues have been marked as duplicates of this issue. This checks incoming duplicate links, not whether this issue is itself a duplicate.

hasErroredAgentSessions.description: Comparator for filtering issues bucketed as having an errored agent session, no active sessions, and no merged agent pull requests.

hasMergedAgentPullRequests.description: Comparator for filtering issues which have agent-session-linked pull requests that were merged.

hasRelatedRelations.description: Whether the issue has a related link in either direction. Blocking links also count as related when either issue is closed; open blocking relationships are covered by hasBlockingRelations and hasBlockedByRelations.

hasSharedUsers.description: Comparator for filtering issues which have been shared with users outside of the team.

hasSuggestedAssignees.description: Comparator for filtering issues which have suggested assignees.

hasSuggestedLabels.description: Comparator for filtering issues which have suggested labels.

hasSuggestedProjects.description: Comparator for filtering issues which have suggested projects.

hasSuggestedRelatedIssues.description: Comparator for filtering issues which have suggested related issues.

hasSuggestedSimilarIssues.description: Comparator for filtering issues which have suggested similar issues.

hasSuggestedTeams.description: Comparator for filtering issues which have suggested teams.

id.description: Matches the issue UUID or human-readable identifier, such as ENG-123. Use number with a team filter when matching only the numeric portion.

labels.description: Conditions on assigned labels. Use some for at least one matching label, every to constrain all labels, or length: { eq: 0 } for unlabeled issues. Separate some conditions in and can require different labels on the same issue.

lastAppliedTemplate.description: Filters that the last applied template must satisfy.

needs.description: Conditions on customer requests linked to the issue. Use some to require a matching request or length to count linked requests.

null.description: Use true to match an unset issue relation, or false to require it to be set. Omit this field when you only want to test the related record’s properties.

number.description: Matches the issue number within its team. Numbers are not unique across teams, so combine this with team when looking for a specific issue.

or.description: Alternative conditions; the issue must match at least one. Other fields at this level must still match. An empty list adds no condition.

parent.description: Conditions on the immediate parent issue. Use null: true to find top-level issues, or an ID condition to find direct sub-issues of one parent.

priority.description: Conditions on the numeric priority: 0 = No priority, 1 = Urgent, 2 = High, 3 = Medium, 4 = Low. Lower nonzero values mean higher priority.

project.description: Conditions on the assigned project. Use null: true for issues without a project; otherwise the project must match the supplied conditions.

projectMilestone.description: Filters that the issues project milestone must satisfy.

reactions.description: Conditions on emoji reactions added directly to the issue. Reactions on its comments are filtered through comments.reactions.

recurringIssueTemplate.description: [ALPHA] Filters that the recurring issue template must satisfy.

releases.description: Conditions on releases linked to the issue. An issue can belong to several releases; use some to require a matching release or length to count them.

sharedWith.description: Filters that users the issue has been shared with must satisfy.

slaBreachesAt.description: Conditions on the SLA deadline. A deadline before now does not by itself mean the SLA was missed; use slaStatus to distinguish unfinished breaches from completed outcomes.

slaStatus.description: Conditions on the current SLA risk or outcome. Use null: true for issues without an SLA status, including canceled issues and issues without an SLA.

snoozedBy.description: Filters that the issues snoozer must satisfy.

snoozedUntilAt.description: Conditions on when the issue’s triage snooze ends. Use null: true for issues without a recorded snooze time.

sourceMetadata.description: Filters that the source must satisfy.

startedAt.description: Conditions on when work started. Use null: true for issues with no recorded start time; moving back to triage, backlog, or an unstarted status clears it.

state.description: Conditions on the issue’s current status. Filter by type, such as started or completed, to match the same workflow category across teams with different status names and IDs.

subscribers.description: Filters that issue subscribers must satisfy.

suggestions.description: Filters that the issue's suggestions must satisfy.

team.description: Filters that the issues team must satisfy.

title.description: Conditions on the issue title. This does not search descriptions or comments.

triagedAt.description: Conditions on when the issue last left triage. The value is unset before triage is completed and after re-entering triage.

contains.description: Matches strings containing this text. Case-sensitive.

containsIgnoreCase.description: Matches strings containing this text, ignoring case.

containsIgnoreCaseAndAccent.description: Matches strings containing this text, ignoring case and accents.

endsWith.description: Matches strings ending with this text. Case-sensitive.

eqIgnoreCase.description: Matches the full string, ignoring case.

in.description: Values to include in the match. For scalar comparisons, matches any listed value. An empty list matches nothing.

neqIgnoreCase.description: Excludes the full string, ignoring case.

nin.description: Values to exclude from the match. For scalar comparisons, an empty list adds no restriction.

notContains.description: Excludes strings containing this text. Case-sensitive.

notContainsIgnoreCase.description: Excludes strings containing this text, ignoring case.

notEndsWith.description: Excludes strings ending with this text. Case-sensitive.

notStartsWith.description: Excludes strings starting with this text. Case-sensitive.

startsWith.description: Matches strings starting with this text, with case preserved.

startsWithIgnoreCase.description: Matches strings starting with this text, ignoring case.

every.description: Applies each string condition to every item. For example, `{ startsWith: "ENG" }` requires a nonempty array whose items all start with `ENG`. The `in` and `nin` operators compare whole sets of values. Cannot be combined with `some`.

length.description: Compares the number of items using nonnegative integers. Empty and missing arrays both have length zero. This condition must match alongside any `some` or `every` condition.

some.description: Requires a matching item for each supplied string condition; different items may satisfy different conditions. For example, `{ eq: "ENG" }` requires an item equal to `ENG`. Use `nin` to exclude arrays containing any value from a list. Cannot be combined with `every`.

archivedAt.description: Conditions on when the issue was archived. Also set includeArchived on the query; a filter alone does not include records excluded by the query’s archive setting.

assignee.description: Conditions on the assigned user. For example, null: true finds unassigned issues, while id: { eq: "user-uuid" } selects one assignee.

attachments.description: Conditions on the issue’s external links. For example, some with a URL or sourceType condition finds issues with at least one matching attachment.

autoArchivedAt.description: Conditions on when the issue was automatically archived. Include archived issues in the query to find them; restoring an issue clears this value.

autoClosedAt.description: Conditions on when the issue was automatically closed after inactivity. The value is cleared when its status changes.

canceledAt.description: Conditions on when the issue entered a canceled or duplicate status. The value is cleared when the issue leaves those status types.

children.description: Conditions on direct sub-issues. Use some for a matching child, every for all children, or length to count them. This does not search all descendants recursively.

comments.description: Conditions on comments linked directly to the issue, including replies. Inline comments on the issue description are linked through documentContent and are not included by this filter.

completedAt.description: Conditions on the recorded completion time. Use null: false to require a completion time, or a date range to find issues completed during that period.

createdAt.description: Filters by creation time. Use a fixed timestamp or a relative duration, such as `{ gte: "-P7D" }` for resources created in the last seven days.

creator.description: Filters that the issues creator must satisfy.

customerCount.description: Conditions on the number of distinct customers with active requests linked to the issue. Requests without a customer record each count separately. Supply one comparison; to apply a range, put separate customerCount conditions in and.

customerImportantCount.description: Conditions on the number of distinct customers with active, important requests linked to the issue. Important requests without a customer record each count separately. Supply one comparison; to apply a range, put separate customerImportantCount conditions in and.

cycle.description: Conditions on the assigned cycle. Use null: true for issues without a cycle or whose team has cycles disabled. Use null: false to require an assigned cycle on a team with cycles enabled. Other cycle comparisons do not require cycles to be enabled.

delegate.description: Filters that the issue's delegated agent must satisfy.

description.description: Conditions on the issue’s stored description text. Use null to find issues without a stored description, or text comparisons to match its contents.

dueDate.description: Conditions on the due date, without a time of day. Use null: true for issues without a due date.

estimate.description: Conditions on the stored numeric estimate in the team’s scale. Use null to find unestimated issues; zero is a separate, explicit estimate.

hasActiveAgentSessions.description: Comparator for filtering issues bucketed as having active agent sessions, no closed agent pull requests, and no merged agent pull requests.

hasBlockedByRelations.description: Whether another issue blocks this issue, with both issues still open. A link with a closed issue counts under hasRelatedRelations instead.

hasBlockingRelations.description: Whether this issue blocks another issue, with both issues still open. A link with a closed issue counts under hasRelatedRelations instead.

hasDismissedAgentSessions.description: Comparator for filtering issues bucketed as having all agent sessions dismissed or closed, and no merged agent pull requests.

hasDuplicateRelations.description: Whether other issues have been marked as duplicates of this issue. This checks incoming duplicate links, not whether this issue is itself a duplicate.

hasErroredAgentSessions.description: Comparator for filtering issues bucketed as having an errored agent session, no active sessions, and no merged agent pull requests.

hasMergedAgentPullRequests.description: Comparator for filtering issues which have agent-session-linked pull requests that were merged.

hasRelatedRelations.description: Whether the issue has a related link in either direction. Blocking links also count as related when either issue is closed; open blocking relationships are covered by hasBlockingRelations and hasBlockedByRelations.

hasSharedUsers.description: Comparator for filtering issues which have been shared with users outside of the team.

hasSuggestedAssignees.description: Comparator for filtering issues which have suggested assignees.

hasSuggestedLabels.description: Comparator for filtering issues which have suggested labels.

hasSuggestedProjects.description: Comparator for filtering issues which have suggested projects.

hasSuggestedRelatedIssues.description: Comparator for filtering issues which have suggested related issues.

hasSuggestedSimilarIssues.description: Comparator for filtering issues which have suggested similar issues.

hasSuggestedTeams.description: Comparator for filtering issues which have suggested teams.

id.description: Matches the issue UUID or human-readable identifier, such as ENG-123. Use number with a team filter when matching only the numeric portion.

labels.description: Conditions on assigned labels. Use some for at least one matching label, every to constrain all labels, or length: { eq: 0 } for unlabeled issues. Separate some conditions in and can require different labels on the same issue.

lastAppliedTemplate.description: Filters that the last applied template must satisfy.

needs.description: Conditions on customer requests linked to the issue. Use some to require a matching request or length to count linked requests.

null.description: Use true to match an unset issue relation, or false to require it to be set. Omit this field when you only want to test the related record’s properties.

number.description: Matches the issue number within its team. Numbers are not unique across teams, so combine this with team when looking for a specific issue.

or.description: Alternative conditions; the issue must match at least one. Other fields at this level must still match. An empty list adds no condition.

parent.description: Conditions on the immediate parent issue. Use null: true to find top-level issues, or an ID condition to find direct sub-issues of one parent.

priority.description: Conditions on the numeric priority: 0 = No priority, 1 = Urgent, 2 = High, 3 = Medium, 4 = Low. Lower nonzero values mean higher priority.

project.description: Conditions on the assigned project. Use null: true for issues without a project; otherwise the project must match the supplied conditions.

projectMilestone.description: Filters that the issues project milestone must satisfy.

reactions.description: Conditions on emoji reactions added directly to the issue. Reactions on its comments are filtered through comments.reactions.

recurringIssueTemplate.description: [ALPHA] Filters that the recurring issue template must satisfy.

releases.description: Conditions on releases linked to the issue. An issue can belong to several releases; use some to require a matching release or length to count them.

sharedWith.description: Filters that users the issue has been shared with must satisfy.

slaBreachesAt.description: Conditions on the SLA deadline. A deadline before now does not by itself mean the SLA was missed; use slaStatus to distinguish unfinished breaches from completed outcomes.

slaStatus.description: Conditions on the current SLA risk or outcome. Use null: true for issues without an SLA status, including canceled issues and issues without an SLA.

snoozedBy.description: Filters that the issues snoozer must satisfy.

snoozedUntilAt.description: Conditions on when the issue’s triage snooze ends. Use null: true for issues without a recorded snooze time.

sourceMetadata.description: Filters that the source must satisfy.

startedAt.description: Conditions on when work started. Use null: true for issues with no recorded start time; moving back to triage, backlog, or an unstarted status clears it.

state.description: Conditions on the issue’s current status. Filter by type, such as started or completed, to match the same workflow category across teams with different status names and IDs.

subscribers.description: Filters that issue subscribers must satisfy.

suggestions.description: Filters that the issue's suggestions must satisfy.

team.description: Filters that the issues team must satisfy.

title.description: Conditions on the issue title. This does not search descriptions or comments.

triagedAt.description: Conditions on when the issue last left triage. The value is unset before triage is completed and after re-entering triage.

contains.description: Matches strings containing this text. Case-sensitive.

containsIgnoreCase.description: Matches strings containing this text, ignoring case.

containsIgnoreCaseAndAccent.description: Matches strings containing this text, ignoring case and accents.

endsWith.description: Matches strings ending with this text. Case-sensitive.

eqIgnoreCase.description: Matches the full string, ignoring case.

in.description: Values to include in the match. For scalar comparisons, matches any listed value. An empty list matches nothing.

neqIgnoreCase.description: Excludes the full string, ignoring case.

nin.description: Values to exclude from the match. For scalar comparisons, an empty list adds no restriction.

notContains.description: Excludes strings containing this text. Case-sensitive.

notContainsIgnoreCase.description: Excludes strings containing this text, ignoring case.

notEndsWith.description: Excludes strings ending with this text. Case-sensitive.

notStartsWith.description: Excludes strings starting with this text. Case-sensitive.

startsWith.description: Matches strings starting with this text, with case preserved.

startsWithIgnoreCase.description: Matches strings starting with this text, ignoring case.

every.description: Applies each string condition to every item. For example, `{ startsWith: "ENG" }` requires a nonempty array whose items all start with `ENG`. The `in` and `nin` operators compare whole sets of values. Cannot be combined with `some`.

length.description: Compares the number of items using nonnegative integers. Empty and missing arrays both have length zero. This condition must match alongside any `some` or `every` condition.

some.description: Requires a matching item for each supplied string condition; different items may satisfy different conditions. For example, `{ eq: "ENG" }` requires an item equal to `ENG`. Use `nin` to exclude arrays containing any value from a list. Cannot be combined with `every`.

hasSharedUsers.description: Comparator for filtering issues which have been shared with users outside of the team.

lastAppliedTemplate.description: Filters that the last applied template must satisfy.

length.description: Conditions on the total number of related issues, independent of some or every. Use eq: 0 to find an empty collection.

needs.description: Conditions on customer requests linked to the issue. Use some to require a matching request or length to count linked requests.

number.description: Matches the issue number within its team. Numbers are not unique across teams, so combine this with team when looking for a specific issue.

or.description: Alternative collection conditions; at least one must match. Other collection clauses at this level still apply. An empty list adds no condition.

parent.description: Conditions on the immediate parent issue. Use null: true to find top-level issues, or an ID condition to find direct sub-issues of one parent.

priority.description: Conditions on the numeric priority: 0 = No priority, 1 = Urgent, 2 = High, 3 = Medium, 4 = Low. Lower nonzero values mean higher priority.

project.description: Conditions on the assigned project. Use null: true for issues without a project; otherwise the project must match the supplied conditions.

projectMilestone.description: Filters that the issues project milestone must satisfy.

reactions.description: Conditions on emoji reactions added directly to the issue. Reactions on its comments are filtered through comments.reactions.

recurringIssueTemplate.description: [ALPHA] Filters that the recurring issue template must satisfy.

releases.description: Conditions on releases linked to the issue. An issue can belong to several releases; use some to require a matching release or length to count them.

sharedWith.description: Filters that users the issue has been shared with must satisfy.

slaBreachesAt.description: Conditions on the SLA deadline. A deadline before now does not by itself mean the SLA was missed; use slaStatus to distinguish unfinished breaches from completed outcomes.

slaStatus.description: Conditions on the current SLA risk or outcome. Use null: true for issues without an SLA status, including canceled issues and issues without an SLA.

snoozedBy.description: Filters that the issues snoozer must satisfy.

snoozedUntilAt.description: Conditions on when the issue’s triage snooze ends. Use null: true for issues without a recorded snooze time.

some.description: Requires at least one related issue to match these conditions. An empty collection does not match.

sourceMetadata.description: Filters that the source must satisfy.

startedAt.description: Conditions on when work started. Use null: true for issues with no recorded start time; moving back to triage, backlog, or an unstarted status clears it.

state.description: Conditions on the issue’s current status. Filter by type, such as started or completed, to match the same workflow category across teams with different status names and IDs.

hasBlockingRelations.description: Whether this issue blocks another issue, with both issues still open. A link with a closed issue counts under hasRelatedRelations instead.

hasDismissedAgentSessions.description: Comparator for filtering issues bucketed as having all agent sessions dismissed or closed, and no merged agent pull requests.

hasDuplicateRelations.description: Whether other issues have been marked as duplicates of this issue. This checks incoming duplicate links, not whether this issue is itself a duplicate.

hasErroredAgentSessions.description: Comparator for filtering issues bucketed as having an errored agent session, no active sessions, and no merged agent pull requests.

hasMergedAgentPullRequests.description: Comparator for filtering issues which have agent-session-linked pull requests that were merged.

hasRelatedRelations.description: Whether the issue has a related link in either direction. Blocking links also count as related when either issue is closed; open blocking relationships are covered by hasBlockingRelations and hasBlockedByRelations.

hasSharedUsers.description: Comparator for filtering issues which have been shared with users outside of the team.

hasSuggestedAssignees.description: Comparator for filtering issues which have suggested assignees.

hasSuggestedLabels.description: Comparator for filtering issues which have suggested labels.

hasSuggestedProjects.description: Comparator for filtering issues which have suggested projects.

hasSuggestedRelatedIssues.description: Comparator for filtering issues which have suggested related issues.

hasSuggestedSimilarIssues.description: Comparator for filtering issues which have suggested similar issues.

hasSuggestedTeams.description: Comparator for filtering issues which have suggested teams.

id.description: Matches the issue UUID or human-readable identifier, such as ENG-123. Use number with a team filter when matching only the numeric portion.

labels.description: Conditions on assigned labels. Use some for at least one matching label, every to constrain all labels, or length: { eq: 0 } for unlabeled issues. Separate some conditions in and can require different labels on the same issue.

lastAppliedTemplate.description: Filters that the last applied template must satisfy.

needs.description: Conditions on customer requests linked to the issue. Use some to require a matching request or length to count linked requests.

null.description: Use true to match an unset issue relation, or false to require it to be set. Omit this field when you only want to test the related record’s properties.

number.description: Matches the issue number within its team. Numbers are not unique across teams, so combine this with team when looking for a specific issue.

or.description: Alternative conditions; the issue must match at least one. Other fields at this level must still match. An empty list adds no condition.

parent.description: Conditions on the immediate parent issue. Use null: true to find top-level issues, or an ID condition to find direct sub-issues of one parent.

priority.description: Conditions on the numeric priority: 0 = No priority, 1 = Urgent, 2 = High, 3 = Medium, 4 = Low. Lower nonzero values mean higher priority.

project.description: Conditions on the assigned project. Use null: true for issues without a project; otherwise the project must match the supplied conditions.

projectMilestone.description: Filters that the issues project milestone must satisfy.

reactions.description: Conditions on emoji reactions added directly to the issue. Reactions on its comments are filtered through comments.reactions.

recurringIssueTemplate.description: [ALPHA] Filters that the recurring issue template must satisfy.

releases.description: Conditions on releases linked to the issue. An issue can belong to several releases; use some to require a matching release or length to count them.

sharedWith.description: Filters that users the issue has been shared with must satisfy.

slaBreachesAt.description: Conditions on the SLA deadline. A deadline before now does not by itself mean the SLA was missed; use slaStatus to distinguish unfinished breaches from completed outcomes.

slaStatus.description: Conditions on the current SLA risk or outcome. Use null: true for issues without an SLA status, including canceled issues and issues without an SLA.

snoozedBy.description: Filters that the issues snoozer must satisfy.

snoozedUntilAt.description: Conditions on when the issue’s triage snooze ends. Use null: true for issues without a recorded snooze time.

sourceMetadata.description: Filters that the source must satisfy.

startedAt.description: Conditions on when work started. Use null: true for issues with no recorded start time; moving back to triage, backlog, or an unstarted status clears it.

state.description: Conditions on the issue’s current status. Filter by type, such as started or completed, to match the same workflow category across teams with different status names and IDs.

suggestions.description: Filters that the issue's suggestions must satisfy.

team.description: Filters that the issues team must satisfy.

title.description: Conditions on the issue title. This does not search descriptions or comments.

triagedAt.description: Conditions on when the issue last left triage. The value is unset before triage is completed and after re-entering triage.

contains.description: Matches strings containing this text. Case-sensitive.

containsIgnoreCase.description: Matches strings containing this text, ignoring case.

containsIgnoreCaseAndAccent.description: Matches strings containing this text, ignoring case and accents.

endsWith.description: Matches strings ending with this text. Case-sensitive.

eqIgnoreCase.description: Matches the full string, ignoring case.

in.description: Values to include in the match. For scalar comparisons, matches any listed value. An empty list matches nothing.

neqIgnoreCase.description: Excludes the full string, ignoring case.

nin.description: Values to exclude from the match. For scalar comparisons, an empty list adds no restriction.

notContains.description: Excludes strings containing this text. Case-sensitive.

notContainsIgnoreCase.description: Excludes strings containing this text, ignoring case.

notEndsWith.description: Excludes strings ending with this text. Case-sensitive.

notStartsWith.description: Excludes strings starting with this text. Case-sensitive.

startsWith.description: Matches strings starting with this text, with case preserved.

startsWithIgnoreCase.description: Matches strings starting with this text, ignoring case.

every.description: Applies each string condition to every item. For example, `{ startsWith: "ENG" }` requires a nonempty array whose items all start with `ENG`. The `in` and `nin` operators compare whole sets of values. Cannot be combined with `some`.

length.description: Compares the number of items using nonnegative integers. Empty and missing arrays both have length zero. This condition must match alongside any `some` or `every` condition.

some.description: Requires a matching item for each supplied string condition; different items may satisfy different conditions. For example, `{ eq: "ENG" }` requires an item equal to `ENG`. Use `nin` to exclude arrays containing any value from a list. Cannot be combined with `every`.

archivedAt.description: Conditions on when the issue was archived. Also set includeArchived on the query; a filter alone does not include records excluded by the query’s archive setting.

assignee.description: Conditions on the assigned user. For example, null: true finds unassigned issues, while id: { eq: "user-uuid" } selects one assignee.

attachments.description: Conditions on the issue’s external links. For example, some with a URL or sourceType condition finds issues with at least one matching attachment.

autoArchivedAt.description: Conditions on when the issue was automatically archived. Include archived issues in the query to find them; restoring an issue clears this value.

autoClosedAt.description: Conditions on when the issue was automatically closed after inactivity. The value is cleared when its status changes.

canceledAt.description: Conditions on when the issue entered a canceled or duplicate status. The value is cleared when the issue leaves those status types.

children.description: Conditions on direct sub-issues. Use some for a matching child, every for all children, or length to count them. This does not search all descendants recursively.

comments.description: Conditions on comments linked directly to the issue, including replies. Inline comments on the issue description are linked through documentContent and are not included by this filter.

completedAt.description: Conditions on the recorded completion time. Use null: false to require a completion time, or a date range to find issues completed during that period.

createdAt.description: Filters by creation time. Use a fixed timestamp or a relative duration, such as `{ gte: "-P7D" }` for resources created in the last seven days.

creator.description: Filters that the issues creator must satisfy.

customerCount.description: Conditions on the number of distinct customers with active requests linked to the issue. Requests without a customer record each count separately. Supply one comparison; to apply a range, put separate customerCount conditions in and.

customerImportantCount.description: Conditions on the number of distinct customers with active, important requests linked to the issue. Important requests without a customer record each count separately. Supply one comparison; to apply a range, put separate customerImportantCount conditions in and.

cycle.description: Conditions on the assigned cycle. Use null: true for issues without a cycle or whose team has cycles disabled. Use null: false to require an assigned cycle on a team with cycles enabled. Other cycle comparisons do not require cycles to be enabled.

delegate.description: Filters that the issue's delegated agent must satisfy.

description.description: Conditions on the issue’s stored description text. Use null to find issues without a stored description, or text comparisons to match its contents.

dueDate.description: Conditions on the due date, without a time of day. Use null: true for issues without a due date.

estimate.description: Conditions on the stored numeric estimate in the team’s scale. Use null to find unestimated issues; zero is a separate, explicit estimate.

hasActiveAgentSessions.description: Comparator for filtering issues bucketed as having active agent sessions, no closed agent pull requests, and no merged agent pull requests.

hasBlockedByRelations.description: Whether another issue blocks this issue, with both issues still open. A link with a closed issue counts under hasRelatedRelations instead.

hasBlockingRelations.description: Whether this issue blocks another issue, with both issues still open. A link with a closed issue counts under hasRelatedRelations instead.

hasDismissedAgentSessions.description: Comparator for filtering issues bucketed as having all agent sessions dismissed or closed, and no merged agent pull requests.

hasDuplicateRelations.description: Whether other issues have been marked as duplicates of this issue. This checks incoming duplicate links, not whether this issue is itself a duplicate.

hasErroredAgentSessions.description: Comparator for filtering issues bucketed as having an errored agent session, no active sessions, and no merged agent pull requests.

hasMergedAgentPullRequests.description: Comparator for filtering issues which have agent-session-linked pull requests that were merged.

hasRelatedRelations.description: Whether the issue has a related link in either direction. Blocking links also count as related when either issue is closed; open blocking relationships are covered by hasBlockingRelations and hasBlockedByRelations.

hasSharedUsers.description: Comparator for filtering issues which have been shared with users outside of the team.

hasSuggestedAssignees.description: Comparator for filtering issues which have suggested assignees.

hasSuggestedLabels.description: Comparator for filtering issues which have suggested labels.

hasSuggestedProjects.description: Comparator for filtering issues which have suggested projects.

hasSuggestedRelatedIssues.description: Comparator for filtering issues which have suggested related issues.

hasSuggestedSimilarIssues.description: Comparator for filtering issues which have suggested similar issues.

hasSuggestedTeams.description: Comparator for filtering issues which have suggested teams.

id.description: Matches the issue UUID or human-readable identifier, such as ENG-123. Use number with a team filter when matching only the numeric portion.

labels.description: Conditions on assigned labels. Use some for at least one matching label, every to constrain all labels, or length: { eq: 0 } for unlabeled issues. Separate some conditions in and can require different labels on the same issue.

lastAppliedTemplate.description: Filters that the last applied template must satisfy.

needs.description: Conditions on customer requests linked to the issue. Use some to require a matching request or length to count linked requests.

null.description: Use true to match an unset issue relation, or false to require it to be set. Omit this field when you only want to test the related record’s properties.

number.description: Matches the issue number within its team. Numbers are not unique across teams, so combine this with team when looking for a specific issue.

or.description: Alternative conditions; the issue must match at least one. Other fields at this level must still match. An empty list adds no condition.

parent.description: Conditions on the immediate parent issue. Use null: true to find top-level issues, or an ID condition to find direct sub-issues of one parent.

priority.description: Conditions on the numeric priority: 0 = No priority, 1 = Urgent, 2 = High, 3 = Medium, 4 = Low. Lower nonzero values mean higher priority.

project.description: Conditions on the assigned project. Use null: true for issues without a project; otherwise the project must match the supplied conditions.

projectMilestone.description: Filters that the issues project milestone must satisfy.

reactions.description: Conditions on emoji reactions added directly to the issue. Reactions on its comments are filtered through comments.reactions.

recurringIssueTemplate.description: [ALPHA] Filters that the recurring issue template must satisfy.

releases.description: Conditions on releases linked to the issue. An issue can belong to several releases; use some to require a matching release or length to count them.

sharedWith.description: Filters that users the issue has been shared with must satisfy.

slaBreachesAt.description: Conditions on the SLA deadline. A deadline before now does not by itself mean the SLA was missed; use slaStatus to distinguish unfinished breaches from completed outcomes.

slaStatus.description: Conditions on the current SLA risk or outcome. Use null: true for issues without an SLA status, including canceled issues and issues without an SLA.

snoozedBy.description: Filters that the issues snoozer must satisfy.

snoozedUntilAt.description: Conditions on when the issue’s triage snooze ends. Use null: true for issues without a recorded snooze time.

sourceMetadata.description: Filters that the source must satisfy.

startedAt.description: Conditions on when work started. Use null: true for issues with no recorded start time; moving back to triage, backlog, or an unstarted status clears it.

state.description: Conditions on the issue’s current status. Filter by type, such as started or completed, to match the same workflow category across teams with different status names and IDs.

subscribers.description: Filters that issue subscribers must satisfy.

suggestions.description: Filters that the issue's suggestions must satisfy.

team.description: Filters that the issues team must satisfy.

title.description: Conditions on the issue title. This does not search descriptions or comments.

triagedAt.description: Conditions on when the issue last left triage. The value is unset before triage is completed and after re-entering triage.

contains.description: Matches strings containing this text. Case-sensitive.

containsIgnoreCase.description: Matches strings containing this text, ignoring case.

containsIgnoreCaseAndAccent.description: Matches strings containing this text, ignoring case and accents.

endsWith.description: Matches strings ending with this text. Case-sensitive.

eqIgnoreCase.description: Matches the full string, ignoring case.

in.description: Values to include in the match. For scalar comparisons, matches any listed value. An empty list matches nothing.

neqIgnoreCase.description: Excludes the full string, ignoring case.

nin.description: Values to exclude from the match. For scalar comparisons, an empty list adds no restriction.

notContains.description: Excludes strings containing this text. Case-sensitive.

notContainsIgnoreCase.description: Excludes strings containing this text, ignoring case.

notEndsWith.description: Excludes strings ending with this text. Case-sensitive.

notStartsWith.description: Excludes strings starting with this text. Case-sensitive.

startsWith.description: Matches strings starting with this text, with case preserved.

startsWithIgnoreCase.description: Matches strings starting with this text, ignoring case.

every.description: Applies each string condition to every item. For example, `{ startsWith: "ENG" }` requires a nonempty array whose items all start with `ENG`. The `in` and `nin` operators compare whole sets of values. Cannot be combined with `some`.

length.description: Compares the number of items using nonnegative integers. Empty and missing arrays both have length zero. This condition must match alongside any `some` or `every` condition.

some.description: Requires a matching item for each supplied string condition; different items may satisfy different conditions. For example, `{ eq: "ENG" }` requires an item equal to `ENG`. Use `nin` to exclude arrays containing any value from a list. Cannot be combined with `every`.

labels.description: Conditions on assigned labels. Use some for at least one matching label, every to constrain all labels, or length: { eq: 0 } for unlabeled issues. Separate some conditions in and can require different labels on the same issue.

lastAppliedTemplate.description: Filters that the last applied template must satisfy.

length.description: Conditions on the total number of related issues, independent of some or every. Use eq: 0 to find an empty collection.

needs.description: Conditions on customer requests linked to the issue. Use some to require a matching request or length to count linked requests.

number.description: Matches the issue number within its team. Numbers are not unique across teams, so combine this with team when looking for a specific issue.

or.description: Alternative collection conditions; at least one must match. Other collection clauses at this level still apply. An empty list adds no condition.

parent.description: Conditions on the immediate parent issue. Use null: true to find top-level issues, or an ID condition to find direct sub-issues of one parent.

priority.description: Conditions on the numeric priority: 0 = No priority, 1 = Urgent, 2 = High, 3 = Medium, 4 = Low. Lower nonzero values mean higher priority.

project.description: Conditions on the assigned project. Use null: true for issues without a project; otherwise the project must match the supplied conditions.

projectMilestone.description: Filters that the issues project milestone must satisfy.

reactions.description: Conditions on emoji reactions added directly to the issue. Reactions on its comments are filtered through comments.reactions.

recurringIssueTemplate.description: [ALPHA] Filters that the recurring issue template must satisfy.

releases.description: Conditions on releases linked to the issue. An issue can belong to several releases; use some to require a matching release or length to count them.

sharedWith.description: Filters that users the issue has been shared with must satisfy.

slaBreachesAt.description: Conditions on the SLA deadline. A deadline before now does not by itself mean the SLA was missed; use slaStatus to distinguish unfinished breaches from completed outcomes.

slaStatus.description: Conditions on the current SLA risk or outcome. Use null: true for issues without an SLA status, including canceled issues and issues without an SLA.

snoozedBy.description: Filters that the issues snoozer must satisfy.

snoozedUntilAt.description: Conditions on when the issue’s triage snooze ends. Use null: true for issues without a recorded snooze time.

some.description: Requires at least one related issue to match these conditions. An empty collection does not match.

sourceMetadata.description: Filters that the source must satisfy.

startedAt.description: Conditions on when work started. Use null: true for issues with no recorded start time; moving back to triage, backlog, or an unstarted status clears it.

state.description: Conditions on the issue’s current status. Filter by type, such as started or completed, to match the same workflow category across teams with different status names and IDs.

subscribers.description: Filters that issue subscribers must satisfy.

suggestions.description: Filters that the issue's suggestions must satisfy.

team.description: Filters that the issues team must satisfy.

title.description: Conditions on the issue title. This does not search descriptions or comments.

triagedAt.description: Conditions on when the issue last left triage. The value is unset before triage is completed and after re-entering triage.

and.description: Collection conditions that must all match. Different some branches can be satisfied by different issues.

attachments.description: Conditions on the issue’s external links. For example, some with a URL or sourceType condition finds issues with at least one matching attachment.

autoArchivedAt.description: Conditions on when the issue was automatically archived. Include archived issues in the query to find them; restoring an issue clears this value.

autoClosedAt.description: Conditions on when the issue was automatically closed after inactivity. The value is cleared when its status changes.

canceledAt.description: Conditions on when the issue entered a canceled or duplicate status. The value is cleared when the issue leaves those status types.

creator.description: Filters that the issues creator must satisfy.

Important requests without a customer record each count separately. Supply one comparison; to apply a range, put separate customerImportantCount conditions in and.

delegate.description: Filters that the issue's delegated agent must satisfy.

description.description: Conditions on the issue’s stored description text. Use null to find issues without a stored description, or text comparisons to match its contents.

dueDate.description: Conditions on the due date, without a time of day. Use null: true for issues without a due date.

estimate.description: Conditions on the stored numeric estimate in the team’s scale. Use null to find unestimated issues; zero is a separate, explicit estimate.

hasBlockedByRelations.description: Whether another issue blocks this issue, with both issues still open. A link with a closed issue counts under hasRelatedRelations instead.

hasBlockingRelations.description: Whether this issue blocks another issue, with both issues still open. A link with a closed issue counts under hasRelatedRelations instead.

hasDismissedAgentSessions.description: Comparator for filtering issues bucketed as having all agent sessions dismissed or closed, and no merged agent pull requests.

hasDuplicateRelations.description: Whether other issues have been marked as duplicates of this issue. This checks incoming duplicate links, not whether this issue is itself a duplicate.

hasErroredAgentSessions.description: Comparator for filtering issues bucketed as having an errored agent session, no active sessions, and no merged agent pull requests.

hasMergedAgentPullRequests.description: Comparator for filtering issues which have agent-session-linked pull requests that were merged.

hasRelatedRelations.description: Whether the issue has a related link in either direction. Blocking links also count as related when either issue is closed; open blocking relationships are covered by hasBlockingRelations and hasBlockedByRelations.

hasSharedUsers.description: Comparator for filtering issues which have been shared with users outside of the team.

hasSuggestedAssignees.description: Comparator for filtering issues which have suggested assignees.

hasSuggestedLabels.description: Comparator for filtering issues which have suggested labels.

hasSuggestedProjects.description: Comparator for filtering issues which have suggested projects.

labels.description: Conditions on assigned labels. Use some for at least one matching label, every to constrain all labels, or length: { eq: 0 } for unlabeled issues. Separate some conditions in and can require different labels on the same issue.

lastAppliedTemplate.description: Filters that the last applied template must satisfy.

length.description: Conditions on the total number of related issues, independent of some or every. Use eq: 0 to find an empty collection.

needs.description: Conditions on customer requests linked to the issue. Use some to require a matching request or length to count linked requests.

number.description: Matches the issue number within its team. Numbers are not unique across teams, so combine this with team when looking for a specific issue.

or.description: Alternative collection conditions; at least one must match. Other collection clauses at this level still apply. An empty list adds no condition.

parent.description: Conditions on the immediate parent issue. Use null: true to find top-level issues, or an ID condition to find direct sub-issues of one parent.

priority.description: Conditions on the numeric priority: 0 = No priority, 1 = Urgent, 2 = High, 3 = Medium, 4 = Low. Lower nonzero values mean higher priority.

sourceMetadata.description: Filters that the source must satisfy.

startedAt.description: Conditions on when work started. Use null: true for issues with no recorded start time; moving back to triage, backlog, or an unstarted status clears it.

suggestions.description: Filters that the issue's suggestions must satisfy.

addedToCyclePeriod.description: Conditions on when the issue joined its cycle. before includes the cycle’s first 24 hours; during covers the remaining time before closure, and after covers times at or after closure.

assignee.description: Conditions on the assigned user. For example, null: true finds unassigned issues, while id: { eq: "user-uuid" } selects one assignee.

attachments.description: Conditions on the issue’s external links. For example, some with a URL or sourceType condition finds issues with at least one matching attachment.

autoArchivedAt.description: Conditions on when the issue was automatically archived. Include archived issues in the query to find them; restoring an issue clears this value.

autoClosedAt.description: Conditions on when the issue was automatically closed after inactivity. The value is cleared when its status changes.

canceledAt.description: Conditions on when the issue entered a canceled or duplicate status. The value is cleared when the issue leaves those status types.

children.description: Conditions on direct sub-issues. Use some for a matching child, every for all children, or length to count them. This does not search all descendants recursively.

comments.description: Conditions on comments linked directly to the issue, including replies. Inline comments on the issue description are linked through documentContent and are not included by this filter.

completedAt.description: Conditions on the recorded completion time. Use null: false to require a completion time, or a date range to find issues completed during that period.

creator.description: Filters that the issues creator must satisfy.
